When the circle intercepts the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$

So, we need to substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve the resulting equation for $y$, if possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2}+(y+4)^{2} & =9 \\ (0-4)^{2}+(y+4)^{2} & =9 \\ 16+(y+4)^{2} & =9 \\ (y+4)^{2} & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(y+4)^{2}\ge 0$ for all values of $y,$ there is no $y$ such that $(y+4)^{2}=-7.$ Therefore, the circle does not intercept the $y$-axis at any point, as shown below.
